facts.label: Nunca com present perfect
facts.sub: Use have/has never + particípio para dizer que algo nunca aconteceu na sua vida: I have never seen snow. Com she, he e it, use has never.

facts.label: Nunca
facts.sub: Use have never + particípio para dizer que não viveu algo: I have never seen snow. A frase é afirmativa na forma, mas negativa no sentido. Não use outro not na mesma frase.

facts.label: Has
facts.sub: Com he, she e it, use has never: She has never skied. Com I, you, we e they, use have never: We have never skied. Na fala, use as formas curtas I’ve e she’s.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Have never + participle means no experience in life.
We say “I have never saw snow”.
items.why: We say I have never seen snow.

items.s: Never goes between have and the participle.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Have never + participle means no experience in life. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I have never saw snow”. → Falso (We say I have never seen snow.)
Never goes between have and the participle. → Verdadeiro (Yes: have never done.)

pages.title: A trip to the snow · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot afternoon in Phoenix, and the street is quiet. Dee and Leo sit under a big tree with cold lemonade. A phone shows a photo of a white mountain. Neither of them has been to a very cold place. Dee has just found a cheap trip to Colorado. She wants to tell Leo about her plan.

“Leo, I am going on a trip to Colorado. I have never seen snow!” says Dee. “Really? I have seen snow once, but I have never touched it.” says Leo. “We live in Phoenix, so it is hot all year. I have never worn a winter coat.” says Dee.

paragraphs: “Ha! Okay. I have never built a snowman either. Let’s make one.” says Leo. “Perfect! I have never been so excited about a cold place.” says Dee.
